Applied in 7784767:

- The context's `terminal` getters are now backed by per-axis memos, so width readers (the footer breakpoints) no longer re-run on height-only resizes and vice versa. `dimensions()` is a single object signal with identity equality, so without the memos every resize event re-evaluated every row's conditions on both axes.
- Documented that the context's bare `width` is content width (terminal minus tabs/sidebar/padding), since it now sits next to `terminal.width` and the two are easy to confuse.

Checked and deliberately not changed: no per-row `useTerminalDimensions()` callers remain in the transcript tree (`permission.tsx`/`form.tsx`/composer are singletons, bounded at O(1)); no existing shared dimensions helper exists in `packages/tui/src` to reuse. Possible follow-up outside this PR: memoize the signal per renderer inside `useTerminalDimensions` itself (or an app-level context), which would make all ~29 call sites cheap and this context field unnecessary.

Demo: drive run against this branch. Four replies with assistant footers, then a width sweep 100 → 80 → 60 → 44 → 34 → 27 → 24 → 30 → 40 → 70 → 100 crossing the 28/36-column footer breakpoints in both directions, then a prompt submitted at 44 columns. Footer adapts at every width; zero listener warnings in the TUI logs (the pre-fix baseline warned at 11 mounted footers).

Confirming the same behavior from a second client — Hermes Agent v0.20.4 (OpenAI-compatible SSE streaming), reproduced 2/2 on 2026-08-20 against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true`, model `muse-spark-1.2`. HTTP 200 both times; no `finish_reason` chunk, no `data: [DONE]`.

One piece of evidence not mentioned here yet — a **usage/content mismatch** that suggests missing relayed tokens:

| response id | usage.completion_tokens | content chunks actually delivered |
|---|---|---|
| `resp_6a8689bef239393fbefd4378` | 859 | 1 chunk (~8 visible tokens) |
| `resp_6a868a09f37a566e99134339` | 1074 | 1 chunk (~8 visible tokens) |

The raw SSE also contains many non-standard chunks with `"choices": []` and a trailing `{"choices":[],"cost":"0"}` payload after the usage chunk.

Reading: the model appears to produce far more completion tokens (likely reasoning tokens) than the gateway ever relays as delta chunks — they show up in `usage` but never arrive as content, and the terminal `finish_reason` chunk + `[DONE]` are dropped too. This means strict clients not only retry-loop, they may also be billed (if usage-based) for tokens that were never delivered.

Client-side impact matches the report: strict stream-completion validation treats every turn as a mid-stream drop, triggering continuation retries (Hermes attempts 4x) and producing repeated partial output.

Requesting a reopen, per the cleanup note. Re-verified against `dev` just now — the bug and this fix are both still current:

- `lsp/lsp.ts:213` and `:332` still use `path.parse(file).ext || file`, so for an extensionless file the match key becomes the whole path.
- `lsp/server.ts:1776` still declares `extensions: [".dockerfile", "Dockerfile"]` for the bundled `dockerfile` server — that `"Dockerfile"` entry cannot ever match under the current matcher, so the intent is already in the codebase, it just doesn't work.
- `lsp/client.ts:560` still resolves `languageId` from `path.extname` only, so even once a server attaches it receives `plaintext` and won't analyze the file.
- `lsp/language.ts` still has no bare `Dockerfile` key.

Worth noting the community signal: the overlapping PR #33690 was closed by its own author in favor of this one, since the matcher fix alone leaves the file as `plaintext`. Happy to rebase or split it if that helps review.

Independent confirmation on `dev` @ b155b1569, with a runnable repro since the steps above are a bit abstract.

Project with `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5" }
```

```
opencode serve --port 4199

curl -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:4199/config \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT" \
  -d '{"model":"anthropic/claude-opus-4-5"}'
```

Response is `200 {"model":"anthropic/claude-opus-4-5"}`, but on disk:

```
$ ls $PROJECT
config.json      opencode.json

$ cat $PROJECT/opencode.json      # unchanged
{ "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5" }

$ cat $PROJECT/config.json        # written, never read back
{ "model": "anthropic/claude-opus-4-5" }
```

I hit this independently and wrote the same fix before finding this issue, so I can confirm the approach in #42257 works — writing to the file the loader merges last is the right target, and reading the raw text rather than the loaded config matters, otherwise `{env:}` / `{file:}` placeholders get baked into resolved values on rewrite. I closed my duplicate in favour of #42257.

**Reproducing on 1.18.19 (desktop, Windows)** — the "permissions will omit them from context" claim doesn't hold here.

Setup:
- Project `opencode.jsonc` has `"tools": { "paper-search_*": false, "openviking_*": false, "browsermcp_*": false, ... }` (8 MCP servers)
- `opencode debug config` confirms these are auto-migrated to `permission: { "paper-search_*": "deny", ... }`

Observed:
- The main session still receives **all** MCP tool definitions in its tool list (~40-50k tokens across 8 servers), consistent with @CrystalMethod's source analysis of `llm.ts` (only `ask` tools are stripped; `allow`/`deny` pass through unchanged).
- `permission: deny` does block *execution* (calls are rejected), but the schema is still injected into the model context.

Impact:
- Plugins built on the legacy `tools` behavior (e.g. opencode-mcp-triage, which writes `"servername_*": false` and advertises "0 tokens in main session") silently fail to deliver the claimed token savings on current versions — the deny entries migrate to `permission` and only gate calls.

Question: is this a known limitation or a regression? Is there any supported way to *hide* tool definitions from the model (not just block calls) — e.g. the `hidden` field on `tool.definition` (#23297) — or should we treat schema injection as permanent until a native per-agent tool filter lands?

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #40611: Same "Unknown tool 'search'" error in Code Mode — Executor's nested `tools.search()` resolves against OpenCode's outer Code Mode catalog where it doesn't exist, producing the same circular dead-end error. The root cause framing differs slightly (routing vs. advertised name mismatch), but both point to the same naming inconsistency between what the catalog describes and what the runtime registers.

**Investigated on `v2` (`879766aee7`) — the core claim does not reproduce as described.**

The catalog instructions advertise `search` as a **global function inside Code Mode code**, not as `tools.search`:

- `packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts:15-17` — "Use \`search\` to discover…", rendering `CodeMode.searchSignature`
- `searchSignature` resolves to a bare `search(input: { query, namespace, limit, offset })`, with no `tools.` prefix
- `packages/codemode/src/interpreter/runtime.ts:306` registers `search` as a reserved interpreter global (`SearchFunction`), dispatched at `runtime.ts:2001` via `ToolRuntime.search` (`interpreter/execute.ts:51`)

Verified directly against the v2 runtime:

```ts
const runtime = CodeMode.make({ tools: { ns: { demo } } })
await runtime.execute(`return search({ query: "demo" })`)   // ok: true
await runtime.execute(`return tools.search({ query: "demo" })`) // Unknown tool 'search' (expected — not advertised)
```

**Invalid assumptions in the report:**

- There is no `tools.$codemode.search` registration and no `reservedNamespace` symbol anywhere in `packages/codemode/src` (or anywhere on the v2 tree). The cited `makeSearchTool` is internal wiring for the interpreter-global `search`, not a namespaced tool.
- Nothing in the codebase advertises `tools.search`; `git grep 'tools.search'` matches only the internal interpreter wiring.
- The `Unknown tool 'search'` error only occurs if an agent *chooses* `tools.search` despite the instructions showing the bare-global form.

**Remaining valid kernel:** the error-message advice at `packages/codemode/src/tool-runtime.ts:473` — "Use search to find available tools" — is ambiguous; an agent that just failed calling `tools.search` may not infer it means the bare global. **Suggested fix for maintainers:** reword the hints in `tool-runtime.ts` to e.g. "Call the global `search({ query })` function to find available tools." (and similarly for the stale-signature hint at line ~540), plus update the two expectations in `packages/codemode/test/tool-paths.test.ts`.

Reproduced the same decode failure class from step 4 on a fork binary (`1.18.18`, `opencode serve --port 4096`) against a long-lived dual-layer DB. Evidence below is from the serve's own logs plus a bun:sqlite enumeration that mirrors the server-side decoder exactly.

### 1. The decode failure is DB-wide on `session_message`, not one corrupt session

Harness calibrated to the server's decode path (`packages/core/src/session/history.ts` → `SessionHistory.load`), with `id` and `sessionID` injected from SQL columns exactly as the server does:

- **52,575 of 58,002 `session_message` rows fail decode** under the current `SessionMessage.Message` schema
- The failures are the same V1-shaped row class described here: legacy `{"type":"aborted"}` error objects (pre-tighten error union), rows missing required fields added after they were written (`parentID`, `path`, `mode`, `agent`, `cost`, `tokens`, reasoning-part `time.start`), and rows carrying `role:"synthetic"` that the current schema no longer accepts as a standalone role
- Live endpoint confirmation: `GET /api/session/:id/message` → `500 "failed to decode session message"` for every affected session; serve log shows the rejection at `[N]["info"]["error"]`

### 2. Stronger finding: the projector stopped writing `session_message` entirely (Aug 13)

Fresh sessions created after the V1/V2 split merge have **zero `session_message` rows** — `SessionProjector` (packages/core/src/session/projector.ts) no longer projects that table. So this isn't just "old rows are undecodable": the V2 message table is **write-dead for new sessions and read-dead for old ones**. The table is currently a zombie: 58,002 rows, ~90% undecodable, no new writes.

### 3. Why it's invisible today — and the trigger that makes it user-visible

The app's `detectServerProtocol` (packages/app/src/utils/server-protocol.ts:24-34) returns `"v1"` for any healthy server (`/global/health` → `healthy:true` short-circuits before the v2 probe). All current clients (web UI, mobile SDK, paseo SDK 1.14.46) therefore ride the **legacy** `/session/:id/message` surface and never touch the V2 read path — which is why nothing crashes until a V2-protocol client connects. The moment protocol detection or a client selects v2, **every old session with pre-merge rows 500s**, exactly as step 4 predicts.

### 4. The legacy surface has the same row class — fixed at the data layer, already verified

The same V1-shaped rows also break the **legacy** unlimited fetch (validates every row against `SessionV1.WithParts`), which is the surface mobile/paseo/web actually use. That side was repaired in-place on 2026-08-20 (no fork changes, no migration):

- 13 legacy rows `{"type":"aborted"}` → current writer's `{"name":"MessageAbortedError","data":{"message":"Aborted"}}` (shape verified against 3 post-merge reference rows the 1.18.18 binary itself emits)
- 1,493 assistant rows: backfilled `parentID` (most-recent preceding user message) and `path {cwd,root}` from per-session healthy values
- 13 `role:"synthetic"` rows → reparented as `synthetic:true` text parts onto the preceding user message (matches current writer via reminders.ts; 0 post-merge standalone rows exist)
- 1,333 reasoning parts `time:{created,completed}` → `time:{start,end}`

Result: 13,053 messages + 41,648 parts decode clean (0 failures), both affected sessions return HTTP 200 on unlimited fetch, and the serve reads the DB live per request (no restart required). The repair surface was precisely bounded — **1,506 failing rows across exactly the 2 user-visible sessions**, matching the serve log's rejection indexes.

### Suggested fix direction for the V2 side

Data-level repair of `session_message` is impractical at this scale (52.5K rows) and pointless while the projector is write-dead. The two fork-side options, per this issue's framing:

1. **Decoder tolerance** — map the known legacy

Thanks for the report. This appears to be based on the `dev` branch rather than the current `v2` implementation.

On `v2`, the catalog intentionally advertises bare `search(...)`:

- [`packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2/packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts#L9-L17) renders “Use `search`” and the bare `search` signature.
- [`packages/codemode/src/interpreter/runtime.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2/packages/codemode/src/interpreter/runtime.ts#L298-L306) registers `search` directly in the interpreter global scope.
- [`packages/codemode/src/interpreter/execute.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2/packages/codemode/src/interpreter/execute.ts#L43-L55) wires that global to `tools.search` internally on the host-side runtime; that internal property is not the model-facing call syntax.
- [`packages/codemode/test/codemode.test.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2/packages/codemode/test/codemode.test.ts#L824-L855) verifies direct calls such as `search({ query: "file" })` and `search({})`.

There is no `reservedNamespace` or `tools.$codemode.search` registration in the current `v2` tree. `tools.search(...)` is therefore not the advertised call—the correct Code Mode call is the global `search(...)`.

Confirming this happens outside the web-interface-startup path too — same warning triggers reliably on a local stdio MCP server call, specifically at `getPrompt`.

**Environment**
- opencode 1.18.19, Windows 11 (Bun runtime bundled with opencode)
- Local MCP server: `@opengsd/gsd-core@1.11.0`'s `gsd-mcp-server` (stdio transport, spawned via `command: ["node", "<path>/gsd-mcp-server.js"]`)

**Repro**
1. Register a local stdio MCP server in `opencode.json` (`mcp.<name>.type = "local"`).
2. Trigger a prompt fetch through it (in my case, a `/gsd-*` slash command backed by an MCP `prompts/get` call).
3. Warning fires immediately, UI stalls tens of seconds, then the trace below prints and the session effectively dies.

**Trace**
```
MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 drain listeners added.
type: "drain"
count: 11
    at overflowWarning (node:events:185:19)
    at addListener (node:events:158:22)
    at once (node:events:200:36)
    at <anonymous> (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-vbr5bqtv.js:69:2280)
    at new Promise (1:11)
    at send (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-vbr5bqtv.js:69:2131)
    at <anonymous> (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-vbr5bqtv.js:67:14427)
    at new Promise (1:11)
    at request (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-vbr5bqtv.js:67:12703)
    at getPrompt (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-vbr5bqtv.js:67:29206)
    at ~effect/Utils/internal (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-xx30ejg4.js:8:1579)
    at <anonymous> (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-xx30ejg4.js:25:5339)
    at ~effect/Effect/evaluate (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-xx30ejg4.js:25:5625)
    at runLoop (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-xx30ejg4.js:25:2045)
    at evaluate (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-xx30ejg4.js:25:1435)
```
(full trace continues through `~effect` internals — same shape reported above)

**What I ruled out**
- Not the MCP server itself: calling it by hand over stdio with a raw `initialize` JSON-RPC request responds instantly and correctly, no errors.
- Not a slow-spawn/cold-start issue: same result whether the server is launched via `npx` or a direct `node <path>` command.
- Not specific to that MCP server's tool/prompt catalog size: disabling the MCP server entirely (`mcp.<name>.enabled: false`) removes the warning and the stall completely; re-enabling it (with everything else unchanged) reproduces it every time, consistently at the `getPrompt` call site shown in the trace.

So this looks like listener accumulation in the client-side stdio transport (`send`/`request` in the bundled chunk) specifically on the request path used by `prompts/get`, not something a server implementation can work around. Happy to provide `opencode.json` mcp config or anything else that helps narrow it down.
